question: A 36-year-old patient consulted due to constant, constrictive chest pain radiating to both arms and intensifying in the dorsal decubitus position. On examination, your doctor objectifies that the pain is relieved by sitting with the body forward. After conducting a thorough study of the patient, you are diagnosed with acute idiopathic pericarditis. Point out the FALSE answer:

options.opa: There is no specific test for the diagnosis of idiopathic acute pericarditis, so the diagnosis is one of exclusion.
options.opb: Anticoagulants should be avoided because their use can cause hemorrhage in the pericardial cavity.
options.opc: There is no specific treatment, but bed rest and acetylsalicylic acid may be indicated.
options.opd: You must inform your patient that pericarditis occurs in more than 75% of patients.
